mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined for four consecutive weeks (13.6 to 9.9), indicating households are spending progressively less time at home. This sustained unwinding of home-bound behavior is expected to continue feeding into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as discretionary outings resume.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically from 13.6 to 9.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility of more than 15 points (as seen from -4.6 to -21.0) signals a renewed restriction or advisory event that curtails outdoor and incidental movement, which historically precedes a pullback in retail and recreation visits within two weeks.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -4.6 at t-1w to -21.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS drops more than 15 points but RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the following two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a single-week rebound in WORKPLACES mobility (from -26.0 to -15.6) acts as a short-lag leading indicator for retail recovery, since newly resumed office activity quickly translates into nearby retail visits within one week.
